ideas.cost_estimate: One-time train-pair probe fit is O(P·D) per ridge iteration for P sampled transitions and embedding dimension D; it does not run each training step. The per-step loss adds O(B·D) multiplies for batch size B, negligible beside the baseline encoder/decoder and codebook distance calculations; at 24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps, no additional model forward or assignment is required.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The train-only next-item signal has a concentrated, repeatable set of content axes, and preserving those axes better produces SIDs whose prefixes distinguish items that matter for user choices. Keep it only if repeated training-sequence splits yield stable weights and Stage3 test_R@10 improves over 0.06335 without relying on validation/test interactions to derive weights.
ideas.key_change: Estimate which embedding dimensions carry train-only next-item signal, freeze those weights before RQ-VAE training, and measure reconstruction in the weighted metric. The encoder, codebooks, residual assignment, and one-global-SID-per-item contract otherwise remain unchanged.
ideas.motivation: A content embedding may devote much of its capacity to distinctions that do not help predict what users choose next; uniform reconstruction can spend early SID capacity on those axes and blur distinctions useful for next-item ranking.
ideas.novelty: Unlike item-level demand signatures, transition residuals, or changing the quantizer geometry, this keeps each item represented by its existing content vector and learns a single diagonal metric from train-only next-item prediction, applying it only to reconstruction/quantization error.
risks: The probe can overfit sparse transitions or encode popularity rather than transferable preference; diagonal weights miss useful cross-axis combinations; train/test distribution shift can invalidate the estimated utility; poorly chosen clipping or regularization can make the metric effectively uniform or collapse dimensions.

specification.text: From chronological training sequences form pairs (i,j) of consecutive items; fit ridge logistic regression p(j|i) ∝ exp(b_j + x_i^T W x_j) on training pairs only, with fixed regularization and a held-out train-only split for fitting. Let s_d = mean over sampled pairs of |(x_i)_d (W x_j)_d|; set w_d = clip((s_d+ε)^α / mean_k((s_k+ε)^α), w_min, w_max), then renormalize mean(w)=1. Freeze w and replace each embedding-space squared error ||a-b||² in the RQ-VAE reconstruction loss with Σ_d w_d(a_d-b_d)²; quantizer internals are unchanged. If fitting W is impractical, use a diagonal ridge probe and the same formula.

ideas.title: Weight content axes by train-only next-item utility

ideas.cost_estimate: One offline pass over train adjacencies plus k-means on 24,556 vectors; negligible relative to training. Per-step cost is the baseline RQ-VAE plus first-layer work for 64 extra inputs (under 0.1% for the 512-wide encoder), with no added per-step graph operation. At 24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps, the added computation is effectively constant-factor-negligible; feature construction is paid once.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Within-text-neighborhood variation in directed successor roles is predictive of the next item beyond text similarity. Keep it if held-out Stage3 test_R@10 exceeds 0.06335 and train-only diagnostics show nontrivial successor-profile variation among nearby text items; the strongest supporting observation is improved recall among items sharing a text cluster but differing in successor distributions.
ideas.key_change: Estimate each training item's smoothed distribution over coarse successor-text clusters from adjacent train-only events, compress that distribution into a small vector, and concatenate a low-weight normalized version to its text embedding before RQ-VAE. Freeze this feature before the 3000-epoch optimization; all items, including items without observed transitions, use the same global feature map and quantizer.
ideas.motivation: Items with similar text can play different roles in user trajectories: an item often used as a bridge into one family of next items may not be interchangeable with a visually similar item that is usually an endpoint or repeat. Text-only reconstruction can collapse these behaviourally distinct roles and hurt next-item ranking.
ideas.novelty: This adds a compact directed successor-role signal to the input geometry before ordinary global RQ-VAE quantization. It is not level reordering, graph denoising of embedding residuals, popularity/demand weighting, or separate successor code branches: every item still receives one global SID from one residual quantizer.
risks: Sparse item transitions make profiles noisy despite smoothing; coarse successor clusters may erase useful distinctions; concatenation can distort the reconstruction scale or spend scarce code capacity on noise. The frozen Stage3 model may also fail to exploit the modified SID geometry even if the profiles are informative.

specification.text: Fit K=64 spherical k-means centroids c_k on train-item embeddings, and assign each item j to g(j)=argmin_k ||e_j-c_k||². From each row with nonempty history, count directed adjacency (history[-1]=i,target=j) into A[i,g(j)]. Define p_i=(A[i,:]+alpha*u)/(sum_k A[i,k]+alpha), where u_k is the global train successor-cluster frequency normalized to sum 1 and alpha=5. Let q_i=log(p_i/u+1e-6), center each dimension over train items and divide by its train standard deviation (floor 1e-3), then clip to [-3,3]. Set x_i=[e_i, lambda*q_i] with lambda=0.1*sqrt(mean(e²)/mean(q²)); train existing RQ-VAE on x_i, and export its hard indices for all items. Use zero-count prior p_i=u for unseen items. The extra coordinates are auxiliary geometry only; retain existing collision extension to ensure unique global IDs.

ideas.title: Quantize a train-only directed transition-role residual

ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute successor counts/top-8 edges once in O(number of training transitions); store at most 8 edges per training item. Per update, use at most 8 sampled in-batch edge pairs and one rank-16 projection per participating item, O(B·16d + 8·16), versus the baseline's O(B·3Kd) codebook distance work. At the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps), the only recurring extra work is this small projection/pair loss; no extra full-catalog pass or additional quantizer lookup is required per step.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Train transitions contain stable successor neighborhoods that are not already recoverable from text, and making those neighborhoods share nearby latent representations improves the grouping/prefixes learned by Stage 2. Keep it only if a fixed Stage 3 comparison improves test_R@10 over 0.06335 and train-only diagnostics show stronger retained-edge affinity in latent/SID neighborhoods without a material rise in reconstruction error or ID collisions.
ideas.key_change: Estimate sparse item-to-item successor affinity from training sequences, then train the encoder to make high-affinity item pairs close under a low-rank Mahalanobis metric while retaining the baseline reconstruction and quantization losses. At export, use the same learned encoder and ordinary nearest-codeword assignments for every item.
ideas.motivation: Items that occur as plausible next steps in similar training histories can be recommendation substitutes even when their text embeddings are far apart; a reconstruction-only tokenizer can therefore spend SID distinctions on wording rather than on behaviorally useful neighborhoods.
ideas.novelty: Keep one global, deterministic SID per item and the ordinary residual quantizer, but learn a small behavior-derived metric on its encoder space. This does not add context-dependent IDs, extra tokens, Sinkhorn balancing, or a transition-graph denoising pass over the quantizer inputs.
risks: Sequential adjacency is noisy and exposure/popularity-biased; over-regularization may collapse distinct items or hurt content generalization. Sparse minibatch coverage may make the auxiliary gradient intermittent, and the recommendation benefit may be small if Stage 3 already learns these transitions independently of the SIDs.

specification.text: From train sequences only, count directed adjacent pairs n_ij and outgoing totals n_i. Define a symmetric affinity a_ij = 0.5*[log((n_ij+α)/(n_i+αV) / p_j) + log((n_ji+α)/(n_j+αV) / p_i)] for observed edges, clamp below at zero, retain each item's top m=8 neighbors, and row-normalize to w_ij. Let h_i=U z_i, where z_i is the existing encoder output and U is a learned r×d matrix initialized to the first r rows of identity (r=16). Add L_succ = (1/|E_B|) Σ_(i,j)∈E_B w_ij ||h_i-h_j||², with α=1 and E_B the retained edges whose endpoints occur in the current minibatch (use cached sampled edges if none); optimize L_RQ + λ L_succ, λ=0.05, and do not apply the auxiliary term to validation/test interactions. Maintain the existing assignment and collision-resolution export unchanged.

ideas.title: Tilt quantization toward observed next-item neighborhoods

per_scorer_rationale.scoring_1: A train-only diagonal utility metric is a clear, moderately novel way to align reconstruction with recommendation relevance while preserving the existing item representation and SID contract. The motivation is sound and the probe/weighted loss appear implementable at modest cost. Potential impact is meaningful but uncertain because the signal may reflect popularity, overfit sparse transitions, or be largely redundant with the baseline; stability of weights, metric hyperparameters, and transfer under distribution shift remain unknown.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_2: A frozen, train-only probe to reweight content reconstruction is a clear and relatively differentiated way to allocate quantizer capacity toward predictive dimensions while retaining the existing item representation and SID contract. The motivation is plausible and the probe/loss change is implementable at low cost, but diagonal weights may miss interactions and predictive axes may reflect popularity or split-specific noise; the expected ranking gain is consequently moderate and depends on weight stability and generalization.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_3: Train-only utility-weighted reconstruction is a plausible, relatively contained way to prioritize predictive content directions while preserving the global-SID setup. The probe and weighted loss appear implementable with modest overhead, although estimating a full transition probe may be awkward for sparse/high-dimensional data; the diagonal fallback helps feasibility. Expected gains are moderate and depend on utility signal not being popularity or noise. Uncertainties include repeatability across sequence splits, probe calibration/regularization and clipping choices, and whether downstream gains persist under distribution shift.

per_scorer_rationale.scoring_1: Adding a frozen, directed successor-role profile to content geometry is a distinctive, concrete hypothesis about behavioral roles among text-similar items, with a straightforward offline construction and standard global quantization. It could materially improve recommendation-relevant SID distinctions, though gains depend on profile reliability and Stage 3's ability to use the changed geometry. Uncertainties include sparse/noisy item histories, sensitivity to coarse clusters and scaling, and whether the auxiliary coordinates consume capacity without generalizing.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_2: It explicitly encodes directed successor-role differences as frozen auxiliary item features, a distinct behavioral signal that ordinary text reconstruction may omit, while preserving one global SID and the standard quantizer. Train-only profile construction, smoothing, and concatenation are practical; likely impact is meaningful if within-text-neighborhood role variation is reliable. Main uncertainties are sparse/noisy transitions, loss of information in coarse successor clusters, scale/capacity interference, and whether the downstream model benefits from the resulting geometry.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_3: Explicitly encoding each item's smoothed directed successor-cluster profile captures trajectory role beyond its text, and concatenating frozen train-only features into one global quantizer is a distinct, implementable intervention. The offline counts and clustering are tractable; smoothing and the prior provide a defined treatment for unseen items. It could improve behaviorally meaningful SID distinctions, but value depends on whether coarse successor profiles add signal beyond text and Stage 3. Uncertainties include sparsity/noise, sensitivity to cluster resolution and feature scale, and whether the frozen downstream model can exploit the resulting codes.

per_scorer_rationale.scoring_1: A low-rank learned metric regularized by train-only directed successor affinity is a distinct, behavior-grounded extension that retains ordinary global IDs and quantization. The motivation is plausible and the expected compute is manageable, but implementation and optimization are more involved than a frozen feature or metric, especially for edge sampling/minibatch coverage. It could improve behavioral neighborhoods, while risks include exposure-biased or noisy edges, latent collapse, intermittent gradients, and little benefit if Stage 3 independently captures transitions; edge sampling and regularization effectiveness are uncertain.
per_scorer_rationale.scoring_2: A low-rank latent metric regularized by sparse, train-only successor affinity is a plausible route to behavior-aware SID neighborhoods and is meaningfully different from adding explicit successor-profile coordinates. Its scientific rationale and potential ranking impact are strong, but implementation and optimization are less certain: the affinity is exposure-biased, the specified smoothed PMI-style score may be unstable for rare edges, minibatch edge coverage can yield intermittent gradients, and the auxiliary loss could collapse useful content distinctions. It is related to the transition-role feature idea, so experimental distinctness is somewhat lower; the key uncertainty is whether the regularizer adds signal beyond Stage 3 learning transitions itself.

objective: Improve next-item recommendation accuracy over the best recorded Stage3 result (test_R@10 0.06335) by changing how item semantic IDs are built in Stage 2. The mechanism must be affordable at the frozen scale: 24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs on one GPU, so the per-step cost has to stay close to the baseline RQ-VAE. Prefer cheap, well-motivated changes to the semantic-ID geometry or assignment that can be justified from train-only behaviour data, and that keep every item on one global Semantic ID.
